title: Run the full workspace gate matrix cold
description:
The final gate before merge.

  pnpm run test:ci --skip-nx-cache

which is nx run-many --targets=test:sherif,test:knip,test:docs,test:eslint,test:lib,
test:types,test:build,build. Force one COLD run — nx caching will otherwise short-circuit
most of it and can hide a failure that only appears from a clean state.

Then confirm the PR-shaped run too, since it differs:

  pnpm run test:pr

test:pr uses `nx affected` and, importantly, does NOT carry the --exclude=examples/**
that the root test:types / test:build / build scripts do. So example type-check and build
ARE merge gates — a green test:ci is not sufficient evidence on its own.

If anything outside packages/solid-form and examples/solid/* fails, stop and investigate
rather than patching: the port is not supposed to affect any other package, and a failure
there means peer dedupe moved something the resolution invariants in task 1.7 were
supposed to have caught.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test:ci passes from a cold cache; pnpm test:pr passes; no package outside packages/solid-form and examples/solid/* required any change to make them pass.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-04, before this issue is worked, while gating form-1og.2.

A cold full test:ci at nx's configured "parallel": 5 (nx.json:6) FAILS on this 8-core box, and
the failure is pure resource starvation rather than a regression. This issue explicitly calls for
`--skip-nx-cache`, so it will hit this every time. Plan for it.

Observed, cold, parallel=5 -- five packages' test:lib failed together:
  @tanstack/react-form, @tanstack/lit-form, @tanstack/solid-form, @tanstack/vue-form,
  @tanstack/preact-form
always the same userEvent-driven tests ("preserves field state", "should handle submitting
properly", "should (not) validate on change if isTouched is ...", "should not lose focus on
update with withFieldGroup"), diagnosing as "Test timed out in 5000ms" and, unmistakably:
  expected 'FirOstthNearmNeame' to deeply equal 'OtherName'
i.e. 'FirstName' and 'OtherName' interleaved char-by-char -- two overlapping userEvent.type runs.

Same set, serial, passes: `nx run-many --target=test:lib --parallel=1 --projects=<the five>`
-> EXIT=0. A subsequent warm `pnpm run test:ci` -> "Successfully ran ... for 57 projects".
nx's own flaky detector then named exactly those five test:lib tasks.

SO: run this issue's cold gate as
  pnpm exec nx run-many --targets=test:sherif,test:knip,test:docs,test:eslint,test:lib,test:types,test:build,build --skip-nx-cache --parallel=2
and do NOT accept a red result from those five test:lib tasks at parallel=5 as a port regression
without first reproducing it serially. Conversely, a failure that SURVIVES --parallel=1 is real.

This matters more after the port, not less: the Solid 2 timing contract is the thing under test,
so a starvation-induced timeout in solid-form:test:lib is exactly the failure most likely to be
misread as a genuine settle()/flush bug.

title: Get solid-form's own gates green
description:
Run each of packages/solid-form's own targets and fix what falls out.

  pnpm --filter @tanstack/form-core run build      # test:* targets dependsOn ^build
  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run test:eslint
  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run test:types
  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run test:lib
  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run build
  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run test:build

Expected ESLint churn beyond the new rule, in descending likelihood:
  1. import/order — every src/*.tsx gains @solidjs/web, which sorts before solid-js
     within the external group. FULLY AUTOFIXABLE:
       pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form exec eslint ./src ./tests --fix
  2. @typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition (type-aware, set to error by the root
     config). Solid 2 tightens several nullability signatures, so a ?. or ?? that was
     necessary under Solid 1 and is now provably redundant becomes an error. Not
     autofixable — expect a handful of manual edits.
  3. no-unused-vars on the removed createComputed / onMount / Index imports. Mechanical.

For test:build, verify @solidjs/web was EXTERNALIZED rather than bundled — a bundled copy
would mean a second template cache and a second event-delegation root in every consumer:

  grep -c "from \"@solidjs/web\"\|from '@solidjs/web'" packages/solid-form/dist/esm/index.js
                                            # expect >= 1 (bare specifier survived)
  grep -c "delegateEvents = \|_\$template" packages/solid-form/dist/esm/index.js
                                            # expect 0
  test -f packages/solid-form/dist/source/index.jsx   # the "solid" condition target

tanstackViteConfig is expected to externalize dependencies + peerDependencies, which is
why @solidjs/web is a peer — but @tanstack/vite-config could not be inspected locally, so
this is a genuine check rather than a formality.
acceptance_criteria: test:eslint, test:types, test:lib, build and test:build all pass for packages/solid-form; @solidjs/web appears as a bare external specifier in dist/esm/index.js and no template/delegateEvents code was bundled; dist/source/index.jsx exists.

title: Fix test:knip for the dependency moves
description:
Two distinct knip failures, from two different causes.

(a) ROOT @solidjs/testing-library BECOMES UNUSED. Its only importers in the entire repo
are packages/solid-form/tests/{test-setup.ts, createField.test.tsx, createForm.test.tsx,
createFormGroup.test.tsx, createFormHook.test.tsx}. knip resolves a workspace's
dependencies up the tree, so the root declaration at package.json:47 currently satisfies
solid-form. Once task 1.1 moves it into packages/solid-form/devDependencies at
1.0.0-beta.2, the root copy has zero importers.

  package.json:47
    -    "@solidjs/testing-library": "^0.8.10",

It must MOVE, not be duplicated — keeping ^0.8.10 at the root alongside 1.0.0-beta.2 in
the package would also trip sherif, which the two ignore flags from 5.2 do not cover.

(b) @solidjs/web IS UNUSED AT THE MOMENT THE TOOLCHAIN COMMIT LANDS, and becomes used
only when task 2.8 introduces `import type { JSX } from '@solidjs/web'`. This is exactly
what table hit (commit 5a334542c, "referenced only via jsxImportSource and compiled
output").

Add in the toolchain epic:

  knip.json
    {
      "$schema": "https://unpkg.com/knip@5/schema.json",
      "ignoreDependencies": ["@tanstack/react-start"],
      "ignoreWorkspaces": ["examples/**"],
      "workspaces": {
        "packages/solid-form": {
          "ignoreDependencies": ["@solidjs/web"]
        }
      }
    }

and REMOVE the workspaces block again in the commit where 2.8 lands. Skip both if the
toolchain flip and the source port land as a single commit.

Note knip's ignoreWorkspaces: ["examples/**"] means all the example churn is invisible to
it, and knip does not check peerDependencies, so the @solidjs/web peer entry needs
nothing.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm run test:knip passes at every commit of the branch; @solidjs/testing-library appears in exactly one package.json (packages/solid-form); the temporary @solidjs/web ignore is added in the toolchain commit and removed in the commit that introduces the @solidjs/web type import.
notes:
DONE, with part (b) AMENDED -- it turned out to be unnecessary.

(a) AS SPECIFIED. Root package.json's "@solidjs/testing-library": "^0.8.10" deleted; it now
    appears only in packages/solid-form at 1.0.0-beta.2. Moved, not duplicated.

(b) NOT NEEDED. The prescribed workspaces["packages/solid-form"].ignoreDependencies ["@solidjs/web"]
    was added, and knip itself rejected it:
      Configuration hints (2)
      @solidjs/web  packages/solid-form  knip.json  Remove from ignoreDependencies
    knip already counts @solidjs/web as used via tsconfig's jsxImportSource, so the entry was dead
    config from the moment it landed. Removed; the whole `workspaces` block is gone. This also
    deletes the follow-up obligation to strip it again when form-e0p.8 adds the JSX type import.
    Table needed it (commit 5a334542c); this repo does not.

(c) NEW, not in the plan. Root knip.json ignoreDependencies gains "solid-js". form-9j2.7 had to
    add "solid-js": "^1.9.9" to the ROOT package.json to stop pnpm re-resolving the TanStack
    devtools family onto Solid 2 -- it is a resolution anchor with no root importer, so knip
    correctly calls it unused. Read form-9j2.7's notes before touching it; removing either half
    breaks @tanstack/form-example-react-devtools:build.

Final knip.json:
  ignoreDependencies: ["@tanstack/react-start", "solid-js"]
  ignoreWorkspaces:   ["examples/**"]
`pnpm run test:knip` is green. The only remaining output is a pre-existing hint to drop
@tanstack/react-start, which predates this branch, is non-fatal, and is out of scope.
close_reason: Solid 2 toolchain flip landed as one commit; resolution invariants proven after a forced re-resolution

title: Fix test:sherif for the transitional Solid version split
description:
sherif's multiple-dependency-versions rule will fire once the port lands:

  solid-js            2.0.0-beta.30  in packages/solid-form + the 5 migrated examples
                      ^1.9.9         in packages/form-devtools, packages/solid-form-devtools,
                                     and the parked examples/solid/devtools
  vite-plugin-solid   3.0.0-next.21  in packages/solid-form + the 5 migrated examples
                      ^2.11.8        in packages/form-devtools, packages/solid-form-devtools

That split is INTENDED and unavoidable for the duration of the transition — the devtools
family has no Solid 2 line upstream — so the fix is an ignore, not a version alignment.

package.json:19:
  -    "test:sherif": "sherif",
  +    "test:sherif": "sherif --ignore-dependency solid-js --ignore-dependency vite-plugin-solid",

Copied verbatim from /home/kaalin/dev/table/package.json:44 and
/home/kaalin/dev/pacer/package.json:38.

Two things worth knowing:
- sherif does NOT inspect peerDependencies. Proof: packages/form-devtools declares
  >=1.9.9 while packages/solid-form-devtools declares >=1.9.7 and main is green today.
  So the new peer ranges on solid-form are free.
- Parking examples/solid/devtools does remove it from sherif's view (sherif reads
  pnpm-workspace.yaml's packages globs and honours negations), but that alone does NOT
  fix the gate — packages/form-devtools and packages/solid-form-devtools are still
  in-tree Solid 1. The ignore flags are required regardless.

The removal of these flags at Solid 2 GA is tracked in the release epic.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm run test:sherif passes; the ignore flags are limited to solid-js and vite-plugin-solid; a comment or the changeset records that they are transitional and removable once the devtools family ships a Solid 2 line.
notes:
DONE. package.json:19 is now:
  "test:sherif": "sherif --ignore-dependency solid-js --ignore-dependency vite-plugin-solid",

Verified BEFORE the port, on the still-Solid-1 tree: `pnpm run test:sherif` -> "No issues found".
The flags are therefore inert today and become load-bearing only when 9j2.1 lands. That ordering
is deliberate: it means any sherif failure after the flip is a NEW discrepancy, not this one.

ACCEPTANCE, second clause ("a comment or the changeset records that they are transitional"):
package.json is JSON and cannot carry a comment, so the record lives in two places instead --
the commit message body, and bead form-8zl.4, which is the GA cleanup issue and names these exact
two flags as guard #2. form-8zl.1 (the changeset) must also carry a line; noted on that bead.

GATE, and the one thing worth carrying forward: the first run FAILED, and it was not this change.

  NX ... for 57 projects failed
  Failed tasks:
  - @tanstack/react-form:test:lib   - @tanstack/lit-form:test:lib
  - @tanstack/solid-form:test:lib   - @tanstack/vue-form:test:lib
  - @tanstack/preact-form:test:lib

Same handful of tests in five different framework adapters -- "preserves field state",
"should handle submitting properly", "should (not) validate on change if isTouched is ...",
"should not lose focus on update with withFieldGroup". Diagnostics were "Test timed out in
5000ms" plus, decisively:

  expected 'FirOstthNearmNeame' to deeply equal 'OtherName'

which is 'FirstName' and 'OtherName' interleaved character by character -- two userEvent.type
sequences overlapping. That only happens when the event loop is starved; it is not a logic fault,
and a sherif CLI flag cannot reach vue-form's tests in any case.

CAUSE: this is the FIRST genuinely COLD full run on this box. Root package.json is in nx's
sharedGlobals, so editing it invalidated every cached task, and all five heavy user-event suites
executed simultaneously at nx's configured `"parallel": 5` (nx.json:6) on 8 cores. The three
earlier "green" gates (9j2.3, 9j2.2, 9j2.5) all replayed test:lib from cache -- zero occurrences
of "Test timed out" in any of their logs.

PROOF it is contention, not regression:
  nx run-many --target=test:lib --parallel=1 --projects=<the five>  ->  EXIT=0, all pass
  pnpm run test:ci (re-run)  ->  EXIT=0, "Successfully ran targets ... for 57 projects"
and nx's own flaky detector then listed exactly those five test:lib tasks.

Logs: scratchpad/gate-1og.2.log (cold, failed), -retry.log (serial, green), -confirm.log (green).
Consequence for form-1og.5 recorded on that bead: a cold --skip-nx-cache run needs --parallel=2.

title: Solid 2 validation gates
description:
Get every repo gate green against the migrated tree, and add the one lint
rule that guards the port's most dangerous failure mode.

The gate list is nx targets driven from the root package.json:
  test:sherif  test:knip  test:docs  test:eslint  test:lib  test:types  test:build  build

Two of them break for known, intended reasons and need explicit fixes (5.2, 5.3). Three

title: Add the Solid 2 semantic contract suite
description:
New file(s) under packages/solid-form/tests pinning the Solid 2
behaviours this port depends on. This is the epic's real deliverable: the type system
catches NONE of these, and every one of them is a silent failure in production.

Model: /home/kaalin/dev/store/packages/solid-store/tests/solid2-semantics.test.tsx and
/home/kaalin/dev/table/packages/solid-table/tests/unit/solid2Semantics.test.ts.

The seven contracts, in severity order. Each must be verified to FAIL when the specific
fix it guards is reverted — a test that passes either way is worse than no test:

1. OPTIONS LOOP SURVIVES GETTER-FORM OPTIONS (guards M1 / trackOptions).
   createForm(() => ({ get defaultValues() { return sig() } })); change sig; settle();
   assert the form re-seeded. MUST fail with trackOptions deleted from
   createForm/createField/createFormGroup. Highest severity: without it the failure is
   total (every option frozen), silent, and production-visible.

2. NO OWNED-SCOPE WRITE THROWS AND NO REACTIVITY_HALTED.
   Construct a form and fields inside a component body, drive the store, and assert
   console.warn and console.error were never called. This is the ownedWrite/
   REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE regression test.

3. EFFECT-HALF RETURN GUARD (guards M3), IN ITS OWN FILE.
   A single test asserting reactivity still works after an effect whose half returns a
   non-function value. It must be its own file because a REACTIVITY_HALTED failure
   poisons the entire module — colocating it would take the rest of the suite down with
   it and obscure the cause.

4. makeFieldReactive ACTUALLY RE-RENDERS.
   Type a character, settle(), assert the DOM. Plus the issue #1961 property: typing in
   field A must NOT re-render field B. Note this needs the real vitest +
   @solidjs/testing-library environment — a bare Node harness loads two copies of the
   reactive runtime and the JSX insert cannot track the memo.

5. update() NEVER LANDS BEFORE mount() (guards the mounted flag).
   Two <form.Field>s where one's options read a form-state slice the other writes on
   mount; assert api.update is not called before api.mount. This is what { defer: true }
   would NOT have caught.

6. mergeObjects KEEPS A DECLARED DEFAULT (guards 2.2).
   withForm({ props: { title: 'Default' }, render }) rendered as
   <Child form={f} title={undefined} />; assert 'Default' survives. WRITE THIS TEST
   BEFORE choosing mergeObjects over merge, so the choice is evidenced rather than
   asserted — it fails under plain merge and passes under mergeObjects.

7. createFieldGroup.Subscribe UPDATES (guards M5).
   The existing tests at createFormHook.test.tsx:274/:327 assert only the initial value
   and passed while the bug was live. Assert a CHANGE propagates.

Optional but valuable, from solid-pacer's experience: assert the dev-diagnostic
(STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED) count is zero for a representative form. Solid arms strict-read
checking only inside createComponent, so the test must render a NAMED component. Pacer
found real bugs buried under diagnostic noise this way.
acceptance_criteria: a semantic contract suite exists covering all seven contracts; the effect-half return guard is in its own file; each test has been verified to fail when the fix it guards is reverted, and that verification is recorded; the suite passes under test:lib.

title: Migrate tests/createFormHook.test.tsx to Solid 2
description:
707 lines, the largest suite and the one with the most timing-sensitive assertions. Candidates from 3.2: :351 (toHaveFocus after clear+type), :582 and :585 (reactive props through withForm), :622-623, :659 (reactive props through withFieldGroup), :705. :622-623 is the HIGHEST-RISK assertion in the whole suite: await user.click(getByTestId('btn')) expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2) expect(spy).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('loading') It asserts that a createEffect RAN, by call count. Under Solid 2 createEffect is a deferred user effect, so effect call-count assertions are the first thing to break. Note the test itself uses a one-argument createEffect at :592-594 — that is legal in test code (the braced-effect-half lint rule is scoped to src/**), but check whether the one-arg form still tracks as expected under Solid 2, or whether the test should move to the two-arg form to express what it is actually asserting. Also here: this suite has the two createFieldGroup.Subscribe children at :274 and :327 that only ever assert the INITIAL value — {(lastName) =>

{lastName}

} Those are the tests that passed while the M5 staleness bug was live. Since 2.6 changed Subscribe to pass an accessor, these become {(lastName) =>

{lastName()}

}, and they should be STRENGTHENED to assert an update, not just the initial value. That strengthening is what makes the 2.6 fix regression-proof; the semantic suite (3.8 item 7) carries the formal version. And tests/createFormHook.test-d.tsx:4 imports type { JSX } from 'solid-js/jsx-runtime', a subpath that no longer exists — covered in 3.7.
acceptance_criteria: the file passes test:lib; the :274 and :327 Subscribe children call the accessor and assert an UPDATE rather than only the initial value; the :622-623 effect-count assertion is either confirmed working or rewritten to express the same intent under Solid 2 scheduling, with the reason recorded.

title: Migrate tests/createField.test.tsx to Solid 2
description:
628 lines. Same two kinds of change as 3.3.

(1) <Index> -> <For keyed={false}>. Import at :4, uses at :405 and :499.

Note the comment at :404: "{/* Do not change this to For or the test will fail */}".
That refers to Solid 1's KEYED For, which recreates rows on every value change and
breaks the per-row field bindings. keyed={false} is precisely the escape hatch and gives
Index's exact semantics. REWRITE the comment rather than deleting it, e.g.:

  {/* keyed={false} is load-bearing: it gives the Solid 1 <Index> semantics (item
      accessor + stable index). A keyed <For> recreates rows on every value change
      and breaks the per-row form.Field bindings. */}

(2) settle() only where 3.2 proved it necessary. Candidates: :126, :175, :223, :225,
:376, then the array push/remove/submit sequence at :464, :465, :467, :468, :471 and its
object-array variant at :561, :562, :564, :565, :568.

The two <Show>s at :403 and :497 use JSX children — no keyed needed.
acceptance_criteria: no <Index> remains; the ":404 do not change this to For" comment is rewritten to explain keyed={false} rather than deleted; the file passes test:lib; settle() appears only where 3.2 recorded an actual failure.

title: Migrate tests/createForm.test.tsx to Solid 2
description:
644 lines. Two kinds of change.

(1) <Index> is gone from Solid 2. Import at :4 and uses at :505, :563, :615:

  - import { Index, Show, createSignal, onCleanup } from 'solid-js'
  + import { For, Show, createSignal, onCleanup } from 'solid-js'

  - <Index each={...}>{(item, i) => ...}</Index>
  + <For each={...} keyed={false}>{(item, i) => ...}</For>

The keyed={false} overload is children: (item: Accessor<T[number]>, index: number) =>
Element — the SAME callback shape Solid 1's <Index> had. So the callback bodies are
untouched.

(2) settle() only at the sites 3.2 proved need it. Candidates in this file: :42, :113,
:148, :197, :253, :308, :310, :484. Highest risk are :113 (closure variable written by an
async onSubmit — probably wants await waitFor) and :148 (imperative read of a signal
written inside an onMount validator).

Confirmed NOT needing changes: the <Show> at :133-142 uses JSX children rather than a
function child, so Solid 2's non-keyed-function-child-gets-an-accessor change does not
apply. render(() => <Comp />) is unchanged — @solidjs/testing-library@1.0.0-beta.2's
render is a drop-in with the same signature and result shape.
acceptance_criteria: no <Index> remains; every former <Index> is a <For keyed={false}> with an unchanged callback body; the file passes test:lib; settle() appears only where 3.2 recorded an actual failure.

title: Empirical timing pass: run the suite with zero settle() calls
description:
Ordered deliberately BEFORE 3.3-3.6. Run the migrated suite with NOT ONE
settle() added and record exactly which assertions fail. That list is the real timing
contract.

  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run test:lib

DO NOT blanket-insert settle() after every `await user.*`. There are 30 candidate sites;
if 3 of them actually need it, the other 27 calls are 27 pieces of misinformation about
the timing contract, and they bury the ones that matter. Let the failures be the answer.

The 30 candidates, for reference while reading failures — they cluster into three
high-risk shapes:

  HIGHEST RISK
    createForm.test.tsx:113   reads a closure variable written by an ASYNC onSubmit —
                              likely needs await waitFor(...), not settle()
    createForm.test.tsx:148   imperative read of a createSignal accessor written inside
                              an onMount validator — the canonical Solid 2 deferred-read
                              shape
    createFormHook.test.tsx:622-623  expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2) on a
                              createEffect — effect call-count assertions are the first
                              thing to break under deferred scheduling

  createForm.test.tsx      :42, :197, :253, :308, :310, :484
  createField.test.tsx     :126, :175, :223, :225, :376,
                           :464, :465, :467, :468, :471,
                           :561, :562, :564, :565, :568
  createFormHook.test.tsx  :351, :582, :585, :659, :705

createFormGroup.test.tsx has ZERO candidates — it already wraps every post-interaction
assertion in await waitFor(...). It is the model the other three should converge on
wherever settle() is not enough. await waitFor(...) is always safe under Solid 2 because
@testing-library/dom's waitFor polls across macrotask boundaries.

Record the result on this issue AND as a comment in tests/utils/reactive.ts (3.1).
acceptance_criteria: test:lib has been run against the ported source with zero settle() calls added; the set of genuinely failing assertions is recorded on this issue with file:line; the finding is copied into a comment at the top of tests/utils/reactive.ts; no settle() call was added anywhere on the basis of assumption rather than an observed failure.

title: Add the Solid 2 test harness (settle helper)
description:
New file packages/solid-form/tests/utils/reactive.ts, modelled on
/home/kaalin/dev/store/packages/solid-store/tests/utils/reactive.ts:

  import { flush } from 'solid-js'

  /**
   * Drains the Solid 2 reactive queue.
   *
   * Solid 2 defers every update to a microtask (@solidjs/signals: queueMicrotask(flush)),
   * so a value read imperatively in the same synchronous tick as a write returns the
   * previous value. Reads from JSX, memos and effect compute halves need nothing — they
   * re-run when the graph settles.
   *
   * Idempotent, and close to free when the queue is empty.
   *
   * MUST NOT be called from inside onSettled or createTrackedEffect callbacks: flush()
   * is not reentrant there and throws. From an ordinary effect callback it does not
   * throw but is a silent no-op, so it cannot settle reads there either.
   */
  export function settle(): void {
    flush()
  }

Add createEffectTestRoot (also in the store fork's copy) ONLY if the semantic suite in
3.8 needs a disposable root — do not add it speculatively.

Leave tests/utils.ts (the sleep helper) exactly where it is. It is unrelated and is used
by the async-validator tests in createForm.test.tsx and createField.test.tsx. tests/utils/
and tests/utils.ts coexist fine.

No tsconfig change needed: packages/solid-form/tsconfig.json already includes "tests".

title: Solid 2 test suite migration
description:
Migrate packages/solid-form/tests to Solid 2 timing, and pin the timing
contract so the next Solid beta cannot silently break it.

5,600 lines across 4 .test.tsx and 3 .test-d.tsx files. The suite has NO fake timers and
NO flush handling — it relies on `await user.*` plus waitFor, with a number of
synchronous assertions immediately after an await. That assumption is Solid 1's
synchronous effect timing.

returning, so all 43 sync assertions that directly follow a render(...) need nothing at
all. Only the 30 sites that assert synchronously after `await user.*(...)` are
candidates — and those are probably fine too, because Solid schedules via
queueMicrotask while user-event's wait() is setTimeout-backed (a macrotask, which drains
pending microtasks first). Neither reference repo exercises userEvent under Solid 2, so
3.2 settles it empirically rather than by assumption.

is used in tests/createForm.test.tsx and tests/createField.test.tsx. The replacement is

— is IDENTICAL to Solid 1's <Index>. Pure element rename plus the prop.

title: Port createFormHook.tsx to Solid 2
description:
packages/solid-form/src/createFormHook.tsx, 573 lines. Last, because it
holds all the context/props work and depends on the rest being stable. Four changes.

(1) Providers, :354 and :365. The .Provider member does not exist in Solid 2 — the
context object IS the provider component. Note this compiles to
createComponent(undefined, ...), i.e. a RUNTIME CRASH, not a type error, because the
member access is on a Context<T>:

  - <opts.formContext.Provider value={form}>{formProps.children}</opts.formContext.Provider>
  + <opts.formContext value={form}>{formProps.children}</opts.formContext>

  - <opts.fieldContext.Provider value={field}> ... </opts.fieldContext.Provider>
  + <opts.fieldContext value={field}> ... </opts.fieldContext>

(2) splitProps -> omit, :361. omit returns ONLY the rest; read _props.children directly
for the picked half. Signature is variadic: omit(props, ...keys).

  - const [childProps, fieldProps] = splitProps(_props, ['children'])
  + const fieldProps = omit(_props, 'children')
  ...
  - childProps.children(Object.assign(field, opts.fieldComponents))
  + _props.children(Object.assign(field, opts.fieldComponents))

omit returns a live getter-preserving proxy, so the spread into <form.Field> stays
reactive. Reading _props.children inside the <form.Field> children callback rather than
in the untracked body is strictly better than the Solid 1 version.

(3) mergeProps -> mergeObjects, :475 and :563. BOTH sites, not just the config one — see
2.2 for why plain merge is unsafe at :475 too.

  return (innerProps) =>
    createComponent(render as Component<any>, mergeObjects(props ?? {}, innerProps))

  const fieldGroupProps = {
    get form() { return innerProps.form },
    get fields() { return innerProps.fields },
    defaultValues,
    formComponents: opts.formComponents,
  }
  const fieldGroupApi = createFieldGroup(() => fieldGroupProps)
  return createComponent(
    render as Component<any>,
    mergeObjects(props ?? {}, innerProps, { group: fieldGroupApi as any }),
  )

The getters on fieldGroupProps are a small bonus fix: :555-556 currently reads
innerProps.form / innerProps.fields eagerly in an untracked component body, which is a
STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED hit per render. It does not become reactive (createFieldGroup has
no update loop) but the object stays live for FieldGroupApi's own later reads and the
diagnostic goes quiet.

(4) Contexts, :71-73 and :115. Replace the lying casts with honest unions and delete the
two eslint-disable comments at :78 and :120:

  - const fieldContext = createContext<Accessor<AnyFieldApi>>(null as unknown as Accessor<AnyFieldApi>)
  + const fieldContext = createContext<Accessor<AnyFieldApi> | null>(null)
  - const formContext = createContext<AnyFormApi>(null as unknown as AnyFormApi)
  + const formContext = createContext<AnyFormApi | null>(null)

CreateFormHookProps at :152-154 follows: Context<Accessor<AnyFieldApi> | null>,
Context<AnyFormApi | null>.

createComponent, createContext and useContext all stay imported from solid-js — none of
them moved. Only mergeProps and splitProps leave.
design:
On the context sentinels: createContext(null) returns null outside a provider
in Solid 2 and does NOT throw — measured. So the existing null-as-unknown-as-T casts are
not a correctness bug and a minimal port could leave them. Change them anyway: the cast
makes the type lie about a case the code then checks for, which is why both guards need
an eslint-disable for no-unnecessary-condition. With the union, `if (!field) throw`
narrows honestly and the linter is telling the truth.

Do NOT adopt Solid 2's new default-less createContext<T>(), even though it is the
idiomatic form. It throws ContextNotFoundError before useFieldContext can run, which
discards the package's much more useful message ("`fieldContext` only works when within
a `fieldComponent` passed to `createFormHook`"). Both existing throws are already in
component bodies rather than JSX expressions, which is the correct placement — a throw
inside a JSX expression triggers REACTIVITY_HALTED.
acceptance_criteria: both provider tags use the <Context value={...}> form; splitProps is replaced by omit with _props.children read directly; both mergeProps calls use mergeObjects; fieldGroupProps exposes form and fields as getters; both createContext calls take an explicit `| null` union with no casts and the two no-unnecessary-condition eslint-disables are deleted; CreateFormHookProps' Context types match; createComponent/createContext/useContext still come from solid-js.

title: Port createFieldGroup.tsx to Solid 2, and fix Subscribe
design:
Why fix it rather than preserve the value form: Three reasons. (1) The accessor form is already the package's dominant convention and what every test uses for form.Subscribe. (2) It is what the completed solid-pacer port settled on. (3) The value form cannot be made correct without wrapping the child in a memo whose only purpose is to defeat fine-grained updates and re-invoke the whole subtree on every change. If a zero-API-break port were required instead, the compat form is return createMemo(() => functionalUpdate(props.children, data())) — a component may return an accessor, and insert will call it in a tracked scope. It is correct, it just re-renders the whole child. Not recommended: the type change is loud, TS-visible, and one line to migrate ((v) => ...v... becomes (v) => ...v()...). Note the break is SILENT for JS consumers —

{lastName}

would render "function ..." — which is another reason to make it loud in the changeset.
acceptance_criteria: the dead mounted flag is removed; onMount is replaced by onSettled(() => api.mount()); Subscribe passes the accessor to functionalUpdate rather than calling data(); the Subscribe children type takes Accessor<TSelected>; the `as Element` cast is gone; JSX comes from @solidjs/web.

title: Port createField.tsx to Solid 2
description:
packages/solid-form/src/createField.tsx, 749 lines — the largest
reactivity surface in the package and the riskiest single file. Three changes.

(1) makeFieldReactive, :170-215. Replace the Solid 1 "trick Solid into re-rendering"
pattern — createSignal(fieldApi, { equals: false }) plus a createComputed that reads the
seven useSelector accessors purely to register dependencies and then re-emits the same
object identity — with a single memo. Keep the seven useSelector calls at :176-202
exactly as they are.

  /**
   * The FieldApi instance is identity-stable; only its store changes. So the memo
   * exists purely to republish that identity whenever a tracked slice moves, which
   * is what makes `field().state.value` re-render.
   *
   * `equals: false` is load-bearing, not cosmetic: with Solid's default reference
   * equality this memo would recompute and then decline to notify, because it
   * returns the same object every time — downstream would update exactly once, at
   * creation, and never again.
   *
   * Solid 1 did this with createSignal(api, { equals: false }) plus a createComputed
   * that re-emitted the same identity. Under Solid 2 that shape needs
   * ownedWrite: true (the render effect's effect half runs synchronously inside the
   * owned component body) AND a braced effect body (a concise arrow returns the
   * setter's value into the cleanup slot) — two ways to hard-halt the reactive
   * system. A memo has no writer and no cleanup slot, so it has neither.
   */
  return createMemo(
    () => {
      reactiveStateValue()
      reactiveMetaIsTouched()
      reactiveMetaIsBlurred()
      reactiveMetaIsDirty()
      reactiveMetaErrorMap()
      reactiveMetaErrorSourceMap()
      reactiveMetaIsValidating()
      return fieldApi
    },
    { equals: false, name: 'form/field' },
  )

(2) Mount + options loop, :283-303:

  let mounted = false
  /**
   * Instantiates field meta and removes it when unrendered.
   *
   * onSettled replaces Solid 1's onMount, and its RETURN VALUE is the cleanup —
   * onCleanup throws [CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE] inside an onSettled callback, so
   * the nested-onCleanup shape is not portable.
   */
  onSettled(() => {
    const cleanupFn = api.mount()
    mounted = true
    return () => {
      cleanupFn()
      mounted = false
    }
  })

  createRenderEffect(
    () => trackOptions(opts()),
    (nextOptions) => {
      if (!mounted) return
      untrack(() => api.update(nextOptions))
    },
  )

(3) Seeding read, :277:
  - const options = opts()
  + const options = untrack(opts)

Plus imports: drop createComputed/createSignal/onMount, add createMemo,
createRenderEffect, onSettled, untrack, trackOptions; JSX type from @solidjs/web;
JSXElement -> JSX.Element at :569.

createComponent stays imported from solid-js — it did NOT move to @solidjs/web.
design:
Why the memo (option b) and not createSignal + createRenderEffect (option a):

Option (a) works, but it is a live grenade for two independent reasons, both of which
detonate on the FIRST SYNCHRONOUS RUN and both of which produce REACTIVITY_HALTED
(permanent, whole-app):
  - omit ownedWrite: true -> REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, because a render effect's
    effect half runs synchronously inside the owned component body;
  - write the effect half as a concise arrow -> the setter's return value lands in the
    cleanup slot -> "effect callback returned an invalid cleanup value".
Option (b) has no writer at all, so neither failure mode exists. It is also one graph
node instead of two, allocates no tuple per run, and was measured to propagate to
consumers within the SAME flush — no added microtask over Solid 1.

Why the mounted flag stays and { defer: true } is NOT a substitute:
  - defer skips only the FIRST run of the effect half. Solid 1 skipped EVERY run until
    onMount. That window is reachable: onSettled fires only after the render queue
    drains, so a sibling field mounting in the same flush can dirty this field's opts()
    dependencies and drive api.update() before api.mount() has run. FieldApi.mount() is
    what assigns info.instance = this; update() writes defaultValue into the form and
    seeds field meta. The flag was added by be7f9bf7 ("chore: fix timing with Solid
    Form") for exactly this timing.
  - And the guard has to live in the effect half anyway, at which point defer is
    redundant: at the setup run, mounted is already false.

Precondition on the memo: it must be created under an owner (an unowned memo tears
against pending values). makeFieldReactive is always reached from a component body, so
this holds — but createField is public, and a module-scope call now silently creates a
leaking, tearing memo where Solid 1 merely no-op'd onMount. Consider solid-table's
createTable.ts dev-warning shape as a follow-up if that turns out to matter.
acceptance_criteria: makeFieldReactive returns a createMemo with { equals: false } that reads all seven selectors and returns fieldApi; no createSignal/setField remains in that function; onMount is replaced by onSettled whose callback RETURNS the cleanup rather than calling onCleanup; the mounted guard is retained in the render effect's effect half; the seeding read at :277 is untracked; every effect half is a braced block; createComponent is still imported from solid-js.

title: Port createForm.tsx to Solid 2
description:
packages/solid-form/src/createForm.tsx, 290 lines. Smallest of the four
primitives and it exercises every pattern the others need, so do it first.

Imports (:2, :12):
  - import { createComputed, onMount } from 'solid-js'
  + import { createRenderEffect, onSettled, untrack } from 'solid-js'
  + import { trackOptions } from './reactivity'
  - import type { JSXElement } from 'solid-js'
  + import type { JSX } from '@solidjs/web'
  and JSXElement -> JSX.Element at :165 and :166.

Body (:281-287), replacing onMount + createComputed:

  onSettled(() => api.mount())

  /**
   * formApi.update should not have any side effects. Think of it like a `useRef`
   * that we need to keep updated every render with the most up-to-date information.
   *
   * createRenderEffect, not createEffect: its effect half runs in the render queue,
   * ahead of ordinary effects and ahead of onSettled — the Solid 2 stand-in for
   * Solid 1's createComputed ordering. Its first run is synchronous, during setup.
   *
   * trackOptions in the compute half is load-bearing — see its doc comment.
   */
  createRenderEffect(
    () => trackOptions(opts?.()),
    (nextOptions) => {
      // untracked: form-core reads option getters in here, and the dev build flags
      // each one as [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] even though the compute half above
      // already subscribed to them.
      untrack(() => api.update(nextOptions))
    },
  )

Note there is deliberately NO mounted guard here — Solid 1's createComputed had none
either, and a render effect's effect half runs synchronously at creation, so the first
push still happens during setup. Keep that asymmetry with createField/createFormGroup.

Also fix the seeding read at :242:
  - const options = opts?.()
  + // untracked: constructor seed only; the render effect below keeps the instance
  + // current. Reading it bare emits STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED once per form.
  + const options = untrack(() => opts?.())

Subscribe at :278-279 is CORRECT AS WRITTEN and needs no change beyond imports — it
passes the ACCESSOR to functionalUpdate, so the child's reads land wherever the child
puts them. This is the same shape solid-pacer's ported Subscribe uses. Do not "fix" it.

FormApi.update early-returns on undefined, and trackOptions(undefined) is a no-op by
construction, so the opts?.() path stays safe.
design:
onSettled(() => api.mount()) is a deliberate BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, not a rename.

onSettled registers its callback's return value as cleanup; onMount discarded it.
FormApi.mount() returns a cleanup on both its branches. Under Solid 1 that return value
was thrown away, so the devtools listeners and the throttled store subscription leaked
for the lifetime of the page. They are now torn down with the component, which matches
what createField, createFormGroup and createFieldGroup already did.

The teardown is devtools-only (a throttleFormState subscription, three formEventClient.on
handlers, a form-unmounted broadcast) — nothing the form needs to keep working. Take it,
and call it out in the changeset as intentional.

Write it as onSettled(() => api.mount()) rather than onSettled(api.mount). Identical
semantics, but it reads as deliberate rather than accidental.
acceptance_criteria: createForm.tsx imports nothing removed in Solid 2; onMount is replaced by onSettled(() => api.mount()); createComputed is replaced by a two-arg createRenderEffect whose compute half calls trackOptions(opts?.()) and whose effect half is a braced block calling untrack(() => api.update(...)); the seeding read at :242 is untracked; JSXElement is gone; Subscribe still passes the accessor, unchanged.

title: Vendor mergeObjects into src/merge-objects.ts
description:
Copy /home/kaalin/dev/table/packages/solid-table/src/merge-objects.ts to
packages/solid-form/src/merge-objects.ts. Take mergeObjects and its isKeyDefined helper
only — flatMerge is not needed here (it exists in table as a decision artifact for an
option-sync-loop this package does not have).

Keep the vendoring rationale comment, and add the form-specific note that @solidjs/web
re-exports the new semantics under the OLD name mergeProps, so nothing in this package
may import either binding from either module.

Why not Solid 2's merge: merge lets a present-but-undefined key OVERRIDE an earlier
defined value. Measured:

  merge({ group: 'DEFAULT', keep: 1 }, { group: undefined, extra: 2 }).group === undefined

whereas omitting the key entirely yields 'DEFAULT'. Both mergeProps call sites in
createFormHook.tsx (:475 and :563) have the same shape — declared defaults, then caller
JSX props — so this is a live bug at both, not just the config-object one:

  withForm({ props: { title: 'Default' }, render })  rendered as
  <Child form={f} title={maybeTitle()} />            where the accessor returns undefined

silently erases the declared default. So :475 is NOT safe with plain merge either; it is
the same failure with the same silence.

The guard in mergeObjects is deliberately KEY definedness, not VALUE definedness, so it
never evaluates a getter while deciding. It also leaves an all-undefined key off the
result entirely rather than defining it as undefined — which matters because a later
object spread would otherwise re-apply that undefined over a default.

Table ships a regression test for exactly the {onChange: undefined}-erases-the-default
bug; the equivalent for this package is in the test epic (semantic suite item 6), and it
should be written BEFORE choosing mergeObjects over merge so the choice is evidenced.
acceptance_criteria: packages/solid-form/src/merge-objects.ts exports mergeObjects with its overload signatures and the isKeyDefined helper; flatMerge is not included; the vendoring rationale comment is present and mentions that @solidjs/web re-exports the new semantics as mergeProps; nothing in packages/solid-form imports merge or mergeProps from solid-js or @solidjs/web.

title: Add src/reactivity.ts with the trackOptions helper
description:
New file packages/solid-form/src/reactivity.ts, mirroring solid-table's
src/reactivity.ts in role. This is what keeps the options push loop alive under Solid 2
(finding M1) and it is a prerequisite for 2.3, 2.4 and 2.5.

  /**
   * Reads every own enumerable property of `options` so that options supplied as
   * getters (`{ get defaultValue() { return signal() } }`) register as
   * dependencies of the surrounding tracked scope.
   *
   * Solid 2 splits effects into a tracked compute half and an untracked effect
   * half. `api.update(options)` belongs in the effect half — it is imperative —
   * but form-core reads the option properties there, where reads subscribe to
   * nothing. Without this the options-push loop runs once and then never again,
   * and Solid's dev build reports it only as `[STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED]`.
   *
   * The spread result is discarded on purpose: `api.update` still receives the
   * ORIGINAL object, so form-core's later reads keep hitting the caller's live
   * getters exactly as they did under Solid 1.
   */
  export function trackOptions<T>(options: T): T {
    if (options !== null && typeof options === 'object') void { ...options }
    return options
  }

Keep the doc comment — it is the only place the reasoning is recorded, and the function
body looks like dead code without it.

Do NOT export this from src/index.tsx. It is an internal helper, and exporting it would
put a Solid-2-implementation detail in the public API surface.

The matching semantic test (options loop survives getter-form options, and fails with
trackOptions deleted) lives in the test epic, not here.
design:
Why a property-touching helper rather than restructuring the effect:

The alternative is to keep api.update inside the tracked compute half, the way Solid 1's
createComputed did. That works but makes the compute half impure — it performs writes
into form-core on every dependency change, which is exactly what Solid 2's split-effect
design is trying to prevent, and it reintroduces the owned-scope-write hazard.

The alternative table chose — a pull-based writable-memo options store — does not apply
here. It works for table because table.options IS an atom that row models read through.
FormApi.update is an imperative core call with real side effects (it conditionally calls
setFieldValue, setFieldMeta and baseStore.setState), so there is nothing to make
pull-based. The push loop stays; it just has to keep tracking.
acceptance_criteria: packages/solid-form/src/reactivity.ts exports trackOptions<T>(options: T): T with the doc comment intact; it touches every own enumerable property and returns the ORIGINAL object, not the spread copy; it is not re-exported from src/index.tsx.

title: Solid 2 adapter source port
description:
Port the ~2,600 lines of Solid binding in packages/solid-form/src to Solid 2.

Almost none of this is logic. @tanstack/form-core is framework-agnostic and works under
Solid 2 untouched; what changes is reactivity glue. The mechanical part is large but
dull (imports, JSXElement, the provider tag). The judgement is concentrated in about a
dozen sites, and three of them are traps that no type will catch:

M1  The obvious options-loop port silently dies. createRenderEffect(() => opts(),
    o => api.update(o)) looks right and is not: the effect half is untracked, opts()
    commonly returns getters, and api.update evaluates them where nothing subscribes.
    The loop runs ONCE and never again — every option frozen at first render, with only
    a dev-mode [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] line to show for it. Solid 1 had no such hole
    because createComputed(() => api.update(opts())) ran update inside the tracked scope.
    Fixed by the trackOptions() helper in 2.1. Highest-severity item in the port.

M2  onCleanup inside an onSettled callback throws [CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE], so the
    existing onMount + nested onCleanup shape at three sites is not portable at all. The
    cleanup must be RETURNED from the onSettled callback.

M3  The Solid 1 createSignal(api, { equals: false }) re-emit trick has two ways to
    hard-kill the app, both on the synchronous first run. Replaced by a memo in 2.4/2.5.

Order: the two new helper files first, then smallest-to-largest so each lands against a
stable base.

Solid 2 facts this port rests on, all measured against the installed
solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30 (not inferred from the guide):

REMOVED from solid-js: createComputed, onMount, batch, observable, mergeProps,
splitProps, Index, Suspense, the JSXElement type, and the solid-js/web and
solid-js/store subpaths.
STILL in solid-js: createComponent, createContext, useContext, createSignal, createMemo,
createEffect, createRenderEffect, onCleanup, untrack, createRoot, createOwner, getOwner,
runWithOwner, Show/Match/Switch/For, and the types Accessor, Component, ParentProps,
Context, Element.
NEW in solid-js: flush, getObserver, onSettled, createTrackedEffect, merge, omit,
isPending, latest.
JSX (the type namespace) now comes from @solidjs/web.

- createEffect/createRenderEffect are two-arg: (compute, effect). The effect half's
  return value is the CLEANUP SLOT; returning a non-function non-undefined value throws
  and permanently halts reactivity (REACTIVITY_HALTED), whole-app. Effect halves must be
  braced blocks.
- A render effect's effect half runs SYNCHRONOUSLY at creation, inside the owned
  component body. An ordinary createEffect's effect half waits for the flush.
- onSettled fires during the flush, AFTER all render-effect effect halves. Its return
  value is registered as owner cleanup.
- The effect half is UNTRACKED. Reactive reads there subscribe to nothing and emit
  [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED].
- Writing a plain signal from an owned scope throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE unless
  the signal was created with { ownedWrite: true }.
- <Ctx.Provider value={v}> becomes <Ctx value={v}>; the .Provider member does not exist.

title: Install, reconcile the lockfile, and assert resolution invariants
description:
Run pnpm install and prove the resolution is what the port assumes. Each
of these greps is an assertion whose failure changes the plan, not a formality.

  # exactly one @solidjs/web in the tree — if >1, a single-copy override is needed
  # after all (table needs one because @solidjs/router pins it; this repo has no router)
  grep -c "^  '@solidjs/web@" pnpm-lock.yaml          # expect 1

  # the devtools family must NOT have been captured by Solid 2. This is the grep that
  # would falsify the semver argument in 1.3 and force nested solid-js overrides.
  grep -n "@tanstack/devtools.*solid-js@2\|@tanstack/solid-devtools.*solid-js@2" pnpm-lock.yaml
                                                      # expect empty

  # the github: dep must survive blockExoticSubdeps: true
  pnpm install 2>&1 | grep -n "ERR_PNPM_EXOTIC_SUBDEP\|TRUST_DOWNGRADE"   # expect empty

  # no unmet peers at all
  pnpm install 2>&1 | grep -i "unmet peer"            # expect empty

Also confirm the lockfile diff is limited to what was intended: the solid-form importer,
the parked examples/solid/devtools importer removal, and the Solid 2 resolutions. A
surprise diff elsewhere means peer dedupe moved something.
design:
Why blockExoticSubdeps: true and trustPolicy: 'no-downgrade' (both set in this
repo's pnpm-workspace.yaml) do not block the github: dependency:

- blockExoticSubdeps only fires at depth > 0. pnpm's guard is
  `ctx.blockExoticSubdeps && options.currentDepth > 0 && isExoticDep(...)`. A github:

title: Silence the @solidjs/testing-library Solid 2 peer warning
description:
@solidjs/testing-library@1.0.0-beta.2 declares peerDependencies of
solid-js >=2.0.0 and @solidjs/web >=2.0.0. node-semver admits a prerelease into a range
only when some comparator in that range shares its [major,minor,patch] tuple, so
">=2.0.0" does NOT match "2.0.0-beta.30" and pnpm reports unmet peers.

Add to pnpm-workspace.yaml (the repo currently has no packageExtensions block at all;
put it after the existing "overrides" line and before "packages:"):

  packageExtensions:
    # Solid 2 transition (remove at Solid 2 GA): @solidjs/testing-library@1.0.0-beta.2
    # declares `>=2.0.0` peers, and semver only admits a prerelease when some
    # comparator in the range shares its [major,minor,patch] tuple — so `>=2.0.0`
    # does not match `2.0.0-beta.30`.
    '@solidjs/testing-library':
      peerDependencies:
        solid-js: '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'
        '@solidjs/web': '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'

Use packageExtensions, NOT the peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions form the store fork
used: allowedVersions only silences the warning, while packageExtensions rewrites the
manifest so pnpm's peer resolver actually selects the Solid 2 copy.

Note this repo runs pnpm 11.3.0, which ignores the "pnpm" field in package.json — all of
this must live in pnpm-workspace.yaml.

DO NOT also add the vite-plugin-solid jest-dom relaxation that table and pacer carry.
They need it because they are on @testing-library/jest-dom 7; this repo pins ^6.8.0,
which already satisfies vite-plugin-solid@3.0.0-next.21's peer of
"^5.16.6 || ^5.17.0 || ^6.*". Adding it would be cargo-culted noise. If, contrary to
this, install reports an unmet jest-dom peer, add it then and note why.
design:
CORRECTED 2026-08-04 by direct measurement — the mechanism this issue originally prescribed cannot work.

pnpm's packageExtensions are PURELY ADDITIVE. They can add keys to a published manifest but cannot replace a key it already declares (the same rule Yarn documents, which pnpm inherits). Measured in an isolated pnpm 11.3.0 workspace: extending @solidjs/testing-library with peerDependencies {left-pad: '*'} produced a lockfile entry reading

  peerDependencies:
    '@solidjs/web': '>=2.0.0'   <- ORIGINAL, not rewritten
    left-pad: '*'               <- added
    solid-js: '>=2.0.0'         <- ORIGINAL, not rewritten

An additive dependency extension also took effect, so the block IS read from pnpm-workspace.yaml — it simply cannot override. Reproduced identically on pnpm 11.3.0 and 11.8.0, and on a clean slate (no node_modules, no lockfile). The packageExtensions blocks in the table and pacer forks are therefore dead weight that never did anything.

More importantly, the premise was wrong in the other direction too: NOTHING needs to steer resolution. With no extension and no rule at all, pnpm already resolves testing-library against the single Solid 2 copy —

  node_modules/.pnpm/@solidjs+testing-library@1.0.0-beta.2_@solidjs+web@2.0.0-beta.30_solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30__solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30/
    node_modules/solid-js -> ../../solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30/node_modules/solid-js

with exactly one solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30 and one @solidjs/web@2.0.0-beta.30 in the store. The unmet peer is a WARNING, not a resolution failure.

So the remaining problem is cosmetic, and peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions — the mechanism this issue originally rejected — is exactly right for it. Verified: with the rule, 'pnpm peers check' reports 'No peer dependency issues found' and the single-copy layout is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm-workspace.yaml contains a packageExtensions block relaxing @solidjs/testing-library's solid-js and @solidjs/web peers to '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0', with a comment marking it removable at Solid 2 GA; pnpm install reports no unmet peer for @solidjs/testing-library; no vite-plugin-solid extension was added.
notes:
Implemented as peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions in pnpm-workspace.yaml, not packageExtensions — see the corrected design field. Two entries, '@solidjs/testing-library>solid-js' and '@solidjs/testing-library>@solidjs/web', both '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0', with the measurement written into the comment so the next reader does not re-derive it.

Inert until the flip: 'pnpm install' after the edit is a 409ms no-op with a ZERO-line lockfile diff, which is exactly what execution step 1 wants (workspace guards, no version movement). Note pnpm 11 keeps no packageExtensions/peerDependencyRules checksum in the lockfile, so editing these settings alone never invalidates it — the rule takes effect at the next real re-resolution, i.e. when form-9j2.1 rewrites packages/solid-form/package.json.

Acceptance criterion for 'no unmet peer' is therefore verified in the sandbox now and must be re-verified against the real tree at form-9j2.7. Gate: full 'pnpm test:ci' green, 58 projects, exit 0. prettier --check clean.

The 'do NOT add the vite-plugin-solid jest-dom relaxation' instruction still stands and was followed — this repo is on @testing-library/jest-dom ^6.8.0, which already satisfies vite-plugin-solid@3.0.0-next.21's peer.

title: Write the Solid 2 changeset
description:
New file .changeset/solid-2-migration.md, bump type MAJOR. --- '@tanstack/solid-form': major --- It must record FIVE breaking changes, each with a migration line: 1. Solid 1 is no longer supported. The peer range is >=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0. 2. @solidjs/web is now a REQUIRED PEER alongside solid-js. Solid 2 moved the DOM runtime out of solid-js/web into its own package; install both and keep them on the same version. A second copy means a second template cache and a second event-delegation root, so it must resolve to exactly one copy. 3. IMPERATIVE READS ARE NO LONGER SYNCHRONOUS. Solid 2 settles every update on a microtask, so a form.useSelector(...) or field().state read in the same synchronous tick as a write returns the previous value. Reads from JSX, memos and effect compute functions are unaffected — they re-run when the graph settles — so components need no changes. In practice this shows up in tests and the occasional event handler. Awaiting one microtask is enough. 4. createFieldGroup.Subscribe's children now receive an ACCESSOR, matching createForm.Subscribe. Migration: (v) => ...v... becomes (v) => ...v()... Note the old behaviour was a latent staleness bug (the value was frozen at first render), and the break is SILENT for JS consumers —

{lastName}

renders "function ...". 5. FormApi.mount()'s cleanup now actually runs on unmount. Solid 1's onMount discarded the return value, leaking the devtools listeners and the throttled store subscription for the lifetime of the page. Behaviour change, not a bug fix, so it belongs in the notes. Also worth a migration line even though it is Solid's break rather than ours, because consumers hit it in their own code: is gone; use , which has the identical callback shape. Record the TypeScript floor outcome from task 1.6 here too. Close with a maintainer note: @tanstack/solid-form is in a `fixed` changesets group with @tanstack/form-core and every other adapter, so this major lockstep-bumps all nine. That is intentional only if the whole line moves together; if solid-form is to ship on its own version line, pull it out of the `fixed` array in .changeset/config.json before running `changeset version`.
design:
Why MAJOR and not store's minor: @tanstack/solid-form is at 1.33.3. Dropping an
entire peer major, adding a required peer, and changing read timing is unambiguously
breaking under semver. The store fork used minor because @tanstack/solid-store is at
0.11.0, where minor IS the breaking bump — that is the same decision in a different
version regime, not a different decision. Do not copy store's minor literally.

Why NOT edit .changeset/config.json's fixed group, despite the lockstep bump: the fork
never releases. .github/workflows/release.yml:20 gates the release job on
github.repository_owner == 'TanStack', so on dkkloimwieder/form neither `changeset
version` nor `changeset publish` ever runs. The changeset's only function here is as a
durable, machine-readable record of the break that travels with the branch and is already

  createFormHook.tsx:21-27  import type { Accessor, Component, Context, JSXElement, ParentProps } from 'solid-js'

design:

:484, :658; createFormGroup.tsx:344; createFieldGroup.tsx:70-71) and JSXElement only for

renderer-agnostic and EXCLUDES Node, whereas @solidjs/web's

second, narrower element type into a package that already speaks JSX.Element, for no
benefit.

title: Resolve the TypeScript floor for solid-form under Solid 2
description:
packages/solid-form runs test:types against six TypeScript versions
(test:types:ts54 .. ts59). The store fork's matrix starts at ts56 across all its
packages. It is unknown whether Solid 2's .d.ts files parse under TS 5.4/5.5.

Static evidence says they probably do: the root tsconfig sets skipLibCheck: true, so the
Solid 2 .d.ts files are parsed but not checked, and only parse-level syntax matters. A
grep of all 33 .d.ts files in solid-js/types + @solidjs/web/types for post-5.3 syntax
(`<const T`, `, const T`, ` satisfies `, `using `, `accessor `) returned zero hits;
every "accessor" match was JSDoc prose. NoInfer (TS 5.4) is already used unqualified in
solid-form's own source, so 5.4 is already the effective floor.

What cannot be ruled out statically is a type-level incompatibility that only appears
when solid-form's own JSX is checked against @solidjs/web/jsx-runtime by an older checker.

RESOLVE IT AT THE TOP OF THE FLIP, NOT THE END — the answer changes the package.json
being edited in 1.1. Get a Solid 1 baseline first, then re-run after 1.1/1.4 land:

  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run test:types:ts54
  pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-form run test:types:ts55

Decision matrix:
  both pass
    -> keep both script lines; record "supported TypeScript floor unchanged at 5.4" in
       the changeset.
  either fails, diagnostics point into node_modules/solid-js or node_modules/@solidjs/web
    -> delete lines 21-22 of packages/solid-form/package.json. The dispatcher at line 20,
       pnpm run "/^test:types:ts[0-9]{2}$/", is a glob and adapts with no further edit.
       nx targets are per-package so nothing else moves. Leave the root typescript54 and
       typescript55 devDeps alone — 12 other packages still use them. State the new 5.6
       floor in the changeset. This lands solid-form on the store fork's floor.
  either fails, diagnostics point into packages/solid-form/src
    -> do NOT drop the TS versions. Fix the source. A 5.4 failure in our own code is a
       portability bug of ours, not a Solid 2 constraint.

Scope is packages/solid-form ONLY. Do not touch the other 13 packages' matrices.
acceptance_criteria: test:types:ts54 and ts55 have been run against the Solid 2 tree and the outcome recorded on this issue; packages/solid-form/package.json's test:types:* script list reflects the decision matrix; the root typescript54/typescript55 devDependencies are untouched; no other package's type matrix changed.
notes:
RESOLVED: the TypeScript floor is UNCHANGED at 5.4. Keep test:types:ts54 and ts55. No edit to
packages/solid-form/package.json, no change to the root typescript54/typescript55 devDeps, no
other package's matrix touched. Decision-matrix branch 1.

METHOD -- this issue's design worried that the "after" run would be confounded, because after the
flip but before the source port solid-form/src is Solid 1 shaped and errors regardless. Resolved
by making the measurement DIFFERENTIAL instead of absolute: run ts54, ts55 and ts59 against the
same Solid 2 tree and compare. The un-ported source is then a constant that cancels out, and the
only thing the comparison can reveal is a compiler-version difference.

RESULT, all three against Solid 2:
  ts54  exit 2, 38 errors, 0 inside node_modules
  ts55  exit 2, 38 errors, 0 inside node_modules
  ts59  exit 2, 38 errors, 0 inside node_modules
  diff(ts54, ts59) = 0 lines      diff(ts55, ts59) = 0 lines
comparing normalized "file(line,col): error TSxxxx" sets. Not merely equal counts -- the sets are
identical. Nothing in solid-js@2's or @solidjs/web@2's .d.ts files fails to parse at 5.4, which is
what the static grep for post-5.3 syntax predicted. Combined with the Solid 1 baseline already
recorded here (all six versions Done), both halves of the probe are now complete.

Logs: scratchpad/ts54.log, ts55.log, ts59.log; normalized sets in e54.txt, e55.txt, e59.txt.

BONUS -- the 38 errors are the source port's exact worklist, and they confirm the plan's findings
rather than contradicting them:

              splitProps  -> onMount is genuinely gone, so form-e0p.3/.6's move to onSettled is
              forced rather than stylistic; splitProps -> omit; mergeProps -> mergeObjects
              (form-e0p.2); Index -> <For keyed={false}>; JSX moves to @solidjs/web (form-e0p.8)
  TS2339 x4   Property 'Provider' does not exist on Context<...>  -> confirms context-as-provider
  TS2724 x4 / TS7006 x14 / TS7027 / TS2344

without vite-plugin-solid, vitest would need resolve.conditions and ssr.resolve.conditions
of ['browser','development'] plus server.deps.inline: [/solid-js/].

With vite-plugin-solid@3 in the config this should be unnecessary — the plugin injects
the conditions itself, including in test mode (verified: its dist sets
conditions = ['solid', ...]). packages/solid-form/vite.config.ts already has
plugins: [solid()], and solid-table's vite.config.ts is a 9-line file with no conditions
block at all, which is the empirical evidence.

This issue is the negative control: confirm the suite genuinely runs against the browser/
development build and not the inert server one. Cheapest check is that a reactive test
actually fails when it should — e.g. temporarily break a selector and confirm the
assertion fails rather than passing vacuously. If tests pass against the server build,
signals never update and many assertions become meaningless.

Close as "confirmed, no config change needed" or add the conditions with a note on why
the plugin was insufficient.
acceptance_criteria: it is confirmed that packages/solid-form/vite.config.ts needs no manual resolve.conditions / ssr.resolve.conditions / server.deps.inline entries, with the evidence recorded — or those entries are added with a note explaining why vite-plugin-solid@3 did not suffice.

title: Follow-up: remove the Solid 2 transition guards at GA
description:
FOUR guards were added purely because Solid 2 is a PRERELEASE and the workspace temporarily spans
two Solid majors. All should be reconsidered once Solid 2 reaches GA and the TanStack devtools
family has a Solid 2 line.

1. pnpm-workspace.yaml `peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions` -- the @solidjs/testing-library peer
   relaxation to '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0' for solid-js and @solidjs/web. Needed only because node-semver
   admits a prerelease into a range only when some comparator shares its [major,minor,patch] tuple
   AND itself carries a prerelease tag; '>=2.0.0' has the tuple but no tag, so 2.0.0-beta.30 does
   not satisfy it. At GA the published peer matches and the block is dead weight.
   CORRECTED 2026-08-04: originally said `packageExtensions`, which cannot work -- pnpm's
   packageExtensions are additive-only. See form-9j2.2's design field. The relaxation is COSMETIC:
   pnpm links its single Solid 2 copy regardless.

2. package.json test:sherif -- `--ignore-dependency solid-js --ignore-dependency vite-plugin-solid`
   (form-1og.2). Masks the intended split between solid-form (+ migrated examples) and the Solid 1
   devtools packages. Gated on form-8zl.2, not on GA alone. When they come off, run `pnpm exec
   sherif` bare first and read the report rather than assuming it is clean.

3. The peer ranges themselves -- '>=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0' in packages/solid-form should become
   '>=2.0.0 <3.0.0' once GA exists, so consumers are not steered at a beta.

4. NEW, added at form-9j2.7 -- root package.json devDependencies "solid-js": "^1.9.9", plus the
   matching "solid-js" entry in root knip.json ignoreDependencies. This is a RESOLUTION ANCHOR,
   not a real dependency: nothing at the root imports Solid. Without it pnpm re-resolves
   @tanstack/devtools and @tanstack/devtools-ui (which declare solid-js only as a '>=1.9.7' PEER)
   onto solid-js@2, and @tanstack/form-example-react-devtools:build fails with
     [commonjs--resolver] Missing "./web" specifier in "solid-js" package
   REMOVE BOTH HALVES TOGETHER, and only once the devtools family ships Solid 2 (form-8zl.2) --
   this one is NOT gated on Solid 2 GA. Falsifying check after removal:
     grep -nE "@tanstack/devtools.*solid-js@2" pnpm-lock.yaml     # must stay empty
     nx run @tanstack/form-example-react-devtools:build           # must stay green
   Do NOT try to replace it with `overrides`, a packageExtensions dependency injection, or
   `dedupePeerDependents: false` -- all three were measured and none binds an auto-installed peer.
   Full evidence is in form-9j2.7's notes.

Also re-check whether the defensive solid-js ^1.9.9 devDep in packages/solid-form-devtools
(form-9j2.3) is still wanted, or should move with that package's own Solid 2 port. Note it is load
bearing today: it is why that package held at 1.9.13 while the unpinned react-devtools chain drifted.
acceptance_criteria: either all three guards are removed and pnpm test:ci is still green, or the issue remains open with the Solid 2 release status recorded.
